description: Washington-only rules checked against the Revised Code of Washington and the Department of Licensing. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines. Washington suspends for counted moving violations rather than a demerit-point total.

questions.q: Washington's statutory maximum on city and town streets is
questions.explanation: RCW 46.61.400(2)(a) sets twenty-five miles per hour on city and town streets. Those maximums may be altered as authorized in RCW 46.61.405, 46.61.410, and 46.61.415.

questions.q: Washington's statutory maximum on county roads is 50 mph. On state highways it is
questions.explanation: RCW 46.61.400(2)(b) sets fifty miles per hour on county roads, and subsection (2)(c) sets sixty miles per hour on state highways, unless a special hazard requires a lower speed or a different maximum is established under the alteration statutes.

questions.q: When passing a marked Washington school or playground crosswalk that is fully posted with standard speed-limit signs, the speed limit is 20 mph. That speed zone extends
options: 300 feet in either direction from the marked crosswalk
Only while a crossing guard is in the roadway
questions.explanation: RCW 46.61.440 makes it unlawful to exceed twenty miles per hour when passing a marked school or playground crosswalk that is fully posted with standard school or playground speed-limit signs. The speed zone at the crosswalk extends three hundred feet in either direction from the marked crosswalk.

questions.q: A Washington driver is guilty of driving under the influence if, within two hours after driving, the alcohol concentration is
questions.explanation: RCW 46.61.502(1)(a) says a person is guilty of driving under the influence if the person drives a vehicle in the state and has, within two hours after driving, an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or higher as shown by analysis of breath or blood. The same section also covers a THC concentration of 5.00 or higher and being under the influence of liquor, cannabis, or any drug.

questions.q: A Washington driver under 21 who has, within two hours after driving, an alcohol concentration of at least 0.02 but less than the 0.08 figure in RCW 46.61.502 is guilty of
options: No offense if the reading is under 0.08
Driving a motor vehicle after consuming alcohol
Aggravated driving under the influence only
questions.explanation: RCW 46.61.503(1) applies to a person under twenty-one who has, within two hours after operating or being in physical control of a motor vehicle, an alcohol concentration of at least 0.02 but less than the concentration specified in RCW 46.61.502.

questions.q: Washington does not use a demerit-point total for this suspension. The Department of Licensing suspends a license for 60 days if the driver is ticketed for
questions.explanation: The Department of Licensing says the license is suspended for 60 days for 6 moving violations in a 12-month period or 7 moving violations in a 24-month period. A one-year probation follows. Another moving violation during probation suspends the license for 30 days for each offense and restarts the one-year probation.

questions.q: Washington treats a driver as a habitual traffic offender when, within a 5-year period, the driver has
questions.explanation: The Department of Licensing says a habitual traffic offender is a driver who, within a 5-year period, has been convicted of 3 or more offenses listed in RCW 46.65.020(1), or found to have been convicted of or committed 20 or more moving violations listed in WAC 308-104-160. If more than one of these offenses is committed within a 6-hour period, they count as one on the first occasion.

questions.q: A second violation of the rules of the road or of intermediate-license restrictions suspends a Washington teen's license for
questions.explanation: The Department of Licensing says a second violation suspends the license for 6 months or until age 18, whichever comes first. A third violation suspends the license until age 18. No restricted license is issued during that suspension.

questions.q: A Washington intermediate license requires the applicant to be at least 16 and to have held an instruction permit for
questions.explanation: RCW 46.20.075 requires the applicant to be at least 16 and to have possessed a valid instruction permit for not less than six months. The applicant must also have at least 50 hours of driving experience, 10 of which were at night, supervised by a person at least 21 who has had a valid driver's license for at least three years.

questions.q: For the first six months after a Washington intermediate license is issued, or until age 18 if that comes first, the holder may not carry
options: More than three passengers of any age
questions.explanation: RCW 46.20.075 says that for the first six months, or until the holder reaches 18, whichever occurs first, the holder may not operate a vehicle carrying any passengers under 20 who are not members of the holder's immediate family. For the remaining period, the holder may not carry more than three passengers under 20 who are not immediate family.

questions.q: A Washington intermediate licensee may not drive between 1 a.m. and 5 a.m. except
options: If the trip is under 10 miles
questions.explanation: RCW 46.20.075 says the holder may not operate a motor vehicle between 1 a.m. and 5 a.m. except when accompanied by a licensed driver who is at least 25, or for school, religious, or employment activities for the holder or a member of the holder's immediate family.

questions.q: Washington intermediate-license restrictions on passengers and nighttime driving also do not block driving at any hour, with passengers, when the driving is
questions.explanation: The Department of Licensing driver guide says an intermediate licensee may drive at any hour, with passengers, for agricultural purposes. It also says the hour and passenger limits end after one year of safe driving without a crash or traffic offense. Penalties for other violations still apply until age 18.

questions.q: Besides alcohol, RCW 46.61.502 treats a driver as under the influence if, within two hours after driving, the THC concentration is
questions.explanation: RCW 46.61.502(1)(b) says a person is guilty of driving under the influence if the person has, within two hours after driving, a THC concentration of 5.00 or higher as shown by analysis of the person's blood.

questions.q: In Washington, what is the youngest age at which you can get a learner's permit for a car?
questions.explanation: Washington issues a learner's permit for a car at 15 years at the earliest.

questions.q: In Washington, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: Washington requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 6 months.

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in Washington complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: Washington requires 50 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.

questions.q: Of a Washington teen's required supervised driving hours, how many must be at night?
questions.explanation: Washington requires at least 10 hours of the supervised driving to be at night.

questions.q: In Washington, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In Washington, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 16 years.

questions.q: During which hours may a newly licensed teen in Washington not drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: Washington restricts provisional drivers from 1 a.m. to 5 a.m., with exceptions such as work or school.

questions.q: In Washington, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: Washington drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 18 years.

questions.q: How many questions are on the Washington car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: The Washington car knowledge test has 40 questions.

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the Washington car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 80% to pass the Washington car knowledge test.

questions.q: In Washington, a driver under 21 breaks the law at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: Washington sets the under-21 limit at 0.02%.

questions.q: In Washington, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in Washington brings a suspension of 1 year.

questions.q: Unless a sign says otherwise, what is the speed limit in a Washington residential district?
questions.explanation: Washington sets 25 mph in residential districts unless another limit is posted.

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in Washington?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in Washington can be posted up to 70 mph for cars.

questions.q: Which best describes Washington's law on drivers using a phone?
options: Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
No statewide ban on phone use or texting
Only texting is banned for all drivers
Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
questions.explanation: Washington: hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers.

questions.q: When is a left turn on a red light allowed in Washington?
options: From a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street
Only from a one-way street onto a one-way street
questions.explanation: In Washington, a left turn on red (after a full stop, where not prohibited) is allowed: from a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street.

questions.q: How is Washington's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: No seat belt law for adults
Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
questions.explanation: Washington seat belt enforcement is primary.

questions.q: What is Washington's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: Washington requires at least $25,000 / $50,000 / $10,000.
